bridge.arrest_rail: continuous: the rail rests on the climber side of the rungs, which the bridge carries; no break over the mouth
bridge.guard: cheek plate between the stiles and the trunk wall over the span (curved, 0.04 m off the wall), so a foot or hand cannot go into the connector gap
bridge.structure: OPEN (unsized): a 1.0-1.7 m two-stile beam carrying a climber at 1.5 g (14.7 N/kg of climber, suit and tool, masses OPEN)

climber_vs_connector_rim.note: the rim is the intersection curve of the r 0.85 connector with the trunk; the climber is 0.65 m off the axis at the 285 deg station, so the rim is where the wall is, not a trap

dock_passage_vs_bridge.note: the bridge sits 90 deg round from the connector axis; a 0.70 m envelope on the trunk axis clears the stiles (the ladder is already there above and below)

climber_figure.note: the figure of he.trunk_climber (hands on the stiles above the shoulder, soles on the rung, arrester on the rail); on the bridge the same pose repeats rung for rung since the bridge carries the same stiles, rungs and rail

upper_run_to_104.9.note: stile pair clear over [dock bridge end, 104.9] against the built openings (minus the bridged dock mouth) plus the three added ones; the run below the bridge is the built ladder

bypass.status: CANDIDATE (PROTOTYPE): continuous by a bridge over the dock mouth; structure, arrester lock and bridge-versus-docking-passage swing are OPEN
